look_here_first: A small decumbent to ascending sharp-pod bundleflower: find 4–6 pairs of pinnae on a COMPLETE bipinnate leaf with a tiny cup-like extrafloral nectary beside the lowest pinnae. Heads have about 6–16 flowers (local descriptions vary); bisexual flowers with 10 stamens. Look for elongated pointed mature pods about 30–50 mm long. Critical comparison with accepted D. virgatus: do not use the historical name D. virgatus var. acuminatus as a separate species.

key_traits.label: Growth flower fruit
key_traits.text: Small sprawling to ascending perennial bundleflower in gravelly/sandy sites; heads relatively few-flowered; narrow pointed pods. Distinguish from broad sickle-podded Illinois bundleflower. Historically called Desmanthus virgatus var. acuminatus; treated here as an accepted species per ITIS.

key_traits.label: Distinguishing characters
key_traits.text: A few-flowered head and pointed linear pod vs usually larger many-flowered heads of velutinus and illinoensis. D. virgatus may overlap in habits and narrow pod shapes; require well-fruited material and corroborating pinnae/stamen characters.

key_traits.label: Shared genus
key_traits.text: Unarmed perennial Fabaceae with compound bipinnate leaves and small brushlike heads, often a petiolar/rachis gland, flat legume pods. Pod structure diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Leaf
key_traits.text: Helically alternate leaves with 4–6 pairs of primary pinnae; each pinna typically with 9–17 pairs of tiny leaflets; cup-like extrafloral nectary next to the proximal primary pinnae.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Headlike short axillary spike with approximately 6–16 flowers; lower often staminate, upper bisexual; bisexual flowers possess 10 free stamens.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Narrow, acuminate, relatively straight mature pods commonly about 30–50 mm long. Measure actual specimens rather than relying only on habit.

key_traits.label: Source context
key_traits.text: UT Austin Williamson County detailed voucher-based description, supplemented by Flora of North Central Texas
